name: Śrī Keśava Bhāratī
text:
## In short

Keśava Bhāratī, the sannyāsī of Kaṭwā from whom the Lord accepted sannyāsa: by a «trick» the Lord first spoke the sannyāsa mantra into his ear, then received it from him; and he gave Him the name **Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya**.

## The sannyāsa at Kaṭwā (Madhya 28)

The Lord told Nityānanda of His desire to take sannyāsa from Śrī Keśava Bhāratī (chapter summary). At Kaṭwā, when Keśava Bhāratī said he understood that the Lord was only honouring the process of accepting a guru to teach people, the Lord answered: «Please do not deceive Me by your illusory words… so that I may become a servant of Kṛṣṇa» (*bhāṣya*).

> prabhu kahe, — «svapne more kona mahājana
> karṇe sannyāsera mantra karila kathana»

«The Lord said, “In a dream some *mahājana* appeared to Me and spoke some sannyāsa mantra in My ear. Please examine whether it is appropriate or not.” Speaking in this way, the Lord spoke the mantra into Keśava Bhāratī's ear. Thus the Lord by trickery made Keśava Bhāratī His disciple, and Keśava Bhāratī was struck with great wonder.» — «This is the best of all mantras. By the mercy of Lord Kṛṣṇa, what is unknown to You?» — and on the Lord's instruction he spoke that same mantra into the Lord's ear (28.155–159). The *bhāṣya*: the Lord first initiated Keśava Bhāratī and then, to teach people, accepted the same mantra from him.

## The name «Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya» (Madhya 28.169–177)

Thinking of a name, he said: «I cannot find such a Vaiṣṇava in the fourteen worlds… Although the disciple of a Bhāratī should be named Bhāratī, that name is not appropriate for Him.» Śuddha-Sarasvatī appeared on his tongue; he placed his hand on the Lord's chest: «You have induced the people of the world to chant the name of Kṛṣṇa, and by inaugurating the movement of saṅkīrtana, You have awakened people's consciousness. Therefore Your name will be Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya. Because of You, everyone will become fortunate.» There were shouts of «Jaya!» and a shower of flowers.

## Afterwards

The Lord gave him love of God, and he set out with the Lord: «I will go with You. I will stay with You and relish the ecstasy of saṅkīrtana» — «Keeping His guru in front, the Lord departed for the forest» (Antya 1.24–25). Later in Nīlācala the Lord asked him whether *jñāna* or *bhakti* was superior, and was jubilant to hear that *bhakti* was superior (Antya 9, chapter summary).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Madhya 28 (with the bhāṣya's summary), 28.154–177; Antya 1.24–25; Antya 9 (chapter summary).

name: Śrī Mādhavendra Purī
text:
## In short

Mādhavendra Purī, «the first sprout» of the tree of devotion, whose body was «imbued with ecstatic love»: he met Nityānanda on His pilgrimage and the two fell unconscious on seeing each other; Advaita, his disciple, celebrated his appearance day.

## Meeting Nityānanda (Ādi 9.154–193)

«By the will of providence He met Śrī Mādhavendra Purī. The body of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī is imbued with ecstatic love of God, and his followers partake of those same sentiments. He did not relish anything other than loving sentiments for Lord Kṛṣṇa.» «When Nityānanda saw Mādhavendra Purī, He was immediately stunned in ecstatic love and fell to the ground unconscious. Seeing Nityānanda, Mādhavendra Purī forgot himself and fell unconscious.» Nityānanda: «Today I have seen the lotus feet of Mādhavendra Purī. By seeing his ecstatic love of God, My life has become successful.» Mādhavendra could not answer, his throat choked with love, and could not release Him from his embrace: «I have never seen such ecstatic love. Wherever such love of God is found, that is my favorite holy place.» They travelled together some days; «he fell unconscious just by seeing a dark cloud»; «Nityānanda considered Mādhavendra to be His guru and nothing less». The *bhāṣya* (9.154): a renowned Vaiṣṇava sannyāsī and spiritual master of the Mādhva-Gauḍīya *sampradāya*, in whom the seed of the desire tree of devotion first fructified (*Caitanya-caritāmṛta* Ādi 9.10).

## His appearance day at Advaita's house (Antya 4.397–424)

«By divine arrangement the auspicious appearance day of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purī arrived. Although there is no difference between Mādhavendra and Advaita, Ācārya Gosāñi was Mādhavendra's disciple.» The book describes him: always decorated with tears, trembling and roaring, so absorbed in Govinda that he danced on the road, sometimes unconscious for six to nine hours — «yet he was most unhappy to see that the world was devoid of devotional service». People knew only the songs of Maṅgala-caṇḍī and the worship of Ṣaṣṭhī and Viṣahari; when he spoke with sannyāsīs they claimed to be Nārāyaṇa, so he found no one to speak with.

## Other mentions

When Paramānanda Purī, his dear disciple, came to Purī, the Lord said: «Today My acceptance of sannyāsa has borne fruit, for Śrī Mādhavendra Purī has manifested before Me» (Antya 3.172).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 9.154–193 (with bhāṣya); Antya 3.172–178; 4.397–424.

name: Paramānanda Purī
text:
## In short

Paramānanda Purī of Trihut, a dear disciple of Mādhavendra Purī: when he came to Nīlācala the Lord danced and said, «Today My acceptance of sannyāsa has borne fruit»; with Svarūpa Dāmodara he was one of the two principal associates of the Lord's last pastimes.

## Birth (Ādi 2.31, bhāṣya)

«Śrīpāda Paramānanda Purī and Śrī Raghupati Upādhyāya appeared at this place [Trihut, Tirabhukti]. They were both disciples of Śrīla Mādhavendra Purīpāda and very intimate associates of Śrīman Mahāprabhu.» (Ādi 1.161, *bhāṣya*: one of the principal disciples of Mādhavendra Purī, the recipient of Mahāprabhu's mercy and respect.)

## «Now I have seen Paramānanda Purī» (Antya 3.167–181)

«After a few days Paramānanda Purī returned after completing his pilgrimage. On seeing Paramānanda Purī from a distance, Lord Gaurāṅga stood up with respect» and danced:

> «Hari! Hari! Now I have seen Paramānanda Purī. Today My eyes and My life have become successful… Today My acceptance of sannyāsa has borne fruit, for Śrī Mādhavendra Purī has manifested before Me.» (3.170–172)

He embraced him and soaked him with tears; Paramānanda Purī forgot himself. «The Lord was greatly pleased to receive Paramānanda Purī, and He kept him as one of His associates… Sri Paramānanda Purī was a dear disciple of Śrī Mādhavendra Purī and was filled with the mellows of ecstatic love.» «Svarūpa Dāmodara and Paramānanda Purī were two of the principal associates in the Lord's final pastimes» (3.181).

## Other mentions

Among the associates who received the devotees of Bengal in Purī (Antya 8.56–61). Antya 10 begins with «the glories of Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara and Śrī Paramānanda Purī» (chapter summary).

## Sources

*Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata* of Vṛndāvana dāsa Ṭhākura, with the *Gauḍīya-bhāṣya* of Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī (English ed. Bhūmipati dāsa / Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi dāsa, 2003). Ādi 1.161, 2.31 (bhāṣya); Antya 3.167–181; 8.56–61; 10 (chapter summary).
